---
title: "Module reference"
---

```python
import geap

model = geap.PowerUtilityModel()
res = model.solve()
res.compare("equity", "bill").premium
```

## The model

| Member | Signature | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `PowerUtilityModel` | `(params=None, *, delta=None, gamma=None, mu=None, sigma=None, rho=None, claims=None)` | Two-state power-utility specification. Defaults to Mehra and Prescott (1985). |
| `.solve` | `(method="grid")` | `PowerUtilityResults`. `analytical` is the same two-state solution. |
| `.simulate` | `(n_samples=200, years=100, *, seed=0, burn_in=20)` | Finite-sample means from the chain. |
| `.replace` | `(**kwargs)` | A new model with some arguments changed. |
| `.claims` | property | `equity`, `bill`, then any extra levered names. |
| `.consumption_growth` | property | The two gross growth rates. |
| `.transition` | property | 2×2 transition matrix. |

`claims={"high": {"phi": 3}}` adds a levered consumption claim.
`equity` defaults to $\phi=1$. `bill` cannot take a `phi`.

## Results

Returns are annualized net rates in percent.

| Attribute | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| `expected_returns` | Unconditional mean net return by claim |
| `volatility` | Unconditional volatility by claim |
| `mean_log_pd` | Mean log price-dividend; NaN for the bill |
| `risk_free` | The bill, same units |
| `summary()` | Formatted table |
| `to_frame()` | One row per claim |
| `compare(long, short)` | Long minus short |

The family lives in `geap.ccapm`. `PowerUtilityModel` is re-exported at
the `geap` root.
